question.text: Under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 and the Maintenance of Records Rules, an AIF (as a reporting entity) must maintain records of which of the following transactions?

answer.text: Only cash transactions exceeding INR 50 lakh; cross-border transfers are reported by authorized dealers only
Only transactions by non-resident investors exceeding INR 1 crore
All transactions, regardless of amount, via Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) only

All cash transactions of more than INR 10 lakh, all integrally-connected series of cash transactions within a month exceeding INR 10 lakh in aggregate, all cross-border wire transfers exceeding INR 5 lakh, and all suspicious transactions regardless of value

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 12 of the PMLA read with the Maintenance of Records Rules, a reporting entity such as an AIF must maintain records of cash transactions exceeding INR 10 lakh, series of integrally-connected cash transactions in a month aggregating to more than INR 10 lakh, cross-border wire transfers exceeding INR 5 lakh, and all suspicious transactions irrespective of value or whether they are in cash. Forged or counterfeit currency transactions are also recordable. The Trap: Option A uses an incorrect INR 50 lakh threshold and wrongly says cross-border transfers are reportable only by authorised dealers. Option B limits the scope to non-resident investors at an arbitrary INR 1 crore threshold. Option C is wrong because it treats Suspicious Transaction Reports as the only record/reporting route; STRs are in addition to the CTR/cross-border wire transfer record-keeping obligations, not a substitute for them. Note: The stem now asks which transactions and records must be maintained, not only "cash" transactions, because the underlying obligation covers cash, integrally-connected series, cross-border wires above INR 5 lakh and all suspicious transactions taken together.
